clue.text: Before match top player returns

indicators.note: Before tells us the player's word comes ahead of the match word

parts.note: a pro is a professional, a top-class player
to match is to fit or suit

explanation.surface: A star player comes back just before a big match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' looks like a verb about the player coming back, but it is the noun: financial returns.
explanation.definitionFit: Returns on an investment are the gain or surplus it brings in.

clue.text: Speaker's turned in wrong direction, walking in Surrey town

indicators.note: a speaker's version is how the words sound when said, not how they are spelt

parts.note: wry means twisted or bent askew; a gait is a manner of walking

explanation.surface: Someone talking about a person who strolled the wrong way round a Surrey town.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, WRY GAIT gives the town's name. REIGATE is a commuter town in Surrey, south of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Reigate is a market town in the county of Surrey in southern England.

clue.text: Son faces actual trouble, admitting one trumped-up charge?

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so one piece goes inside the other
trouble here means stir up or disturb, so the letters of the preceding words are thrown into disorder

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A son is confronted with real problems after confessing to something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' shuffles SON FACES ACTUAL into FALSEACCUSATON, and 'admitting' lets I in near the end. The question mark marks the definition as a description rather than a dictionary synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumped-up charge is an invented one, brought against someone who did not commit the offence.

clue.text: Facing the wrong way, discharge weapon, causing alarm, perhaps

indicators.note: facing the wrong way says the word for discharge is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: to emit is to discharge or give off
piece is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: Someone fires a gun while facing backwards and causes panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facing the wrong way' turns EMIT into TIME. 'alarm' is a noun here, not panic: an alarm clock, an example of the answer, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm clock is one example of a clock or watch, a device for keeping track of the hours.

clue.text: Trial started off with first of offenders brought in

indicators.note: brought in means placed inside the anagrammed letters
off means wrong or not right, so the letters of started are rearranged
first of picks the opening letter of offenders

explanation.surface: A court case got under way once the leading offender was led into the dock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' turns STARTED into RADTEST, and 'brought in' puts O, the first letter of offenders, after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: A road test is a trial of a vehicle, or of a new product, under real working conditions.

clue.text: Take back plot of land — under half an acre

indicators.note: in a down clue, under puts the land piece below the acre piece
half means only two of the four letters of acre are used, here the second pair

parts.note: a tract is an expanse or plot of land

explanation.surface: Someone withdraws an offer on a small field of less than half an acre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes the last two letters of acre, RE; 'under' places TRACT beneath them in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract is to withdraw a statement or promise one has made.

clue.text: Embarrass adult at party

parts.note: A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult
a bash is an informal party

explanation.surface: Showing up a grown-up at a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash someone is to make them feel ashamed or awkward.

clue.text: With ten euros, colonel briefly tours parts of Europe

indicators.note: tours suggests going round, so the letters travel into a new order

parts.note: Col is the short form of colonel

explanation.surface: An army officer carries ten euros on a trip around the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tours' rearranges WITH TEN EUROS plus COL. The answer means the Netherlands, Belgium and Luxembourg.
explanation.definitionFit: The Low Countries are the low-lying lands of north-west Europe: Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg.

clue.text: Be good model for writer

definitions.meaning: to pose steadily for an artist, keeping still in the chair
Edith, Osbert or Sacheverell, the English literary siblings

explanation.definitionFit: To sit well is to pose well for a portrait, and Edith Sitwell was an English poet.

clue.text: Envoy's paper qualification: first in theology

parts.note: a diploma is a certificate awarded for passing a course

indicators.note: first in picks the opening letter of theology

explanation.surface: An ambassador's certificate is headed by a theology award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Envoy's' is the definition plus a link 's (has).
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomat is an official representing a country abroad, as an envoy does.

clue.text: People with talent like keeping grip on office

indicators.note: keeping grip on means holding something inside, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: as means like, in the same way as
dept is the abbreviation for department, a government office

explanation.surface: Gifted people tend to cling on to their jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Adepts are experts, people highly skilled at something.

clue.text: Something cooked in oven crackles intermittently

indicators.note: intermittently means at intervals, so every other letter of crackles is taken

explanation.surface: A dish in the oven pops and crackles now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of crackles.
explanation.definitionFit: A cake is a sweet food baked in an oven.

clue.text: Hope a store can fix child's toy

indicators.note: fix means repair or rearrange, so the letters of the preceding three words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone hopes a shop can repair a child's broken plaything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' is a link word; 'fix' rearranges HOPE A STORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A peashooter is a small tube through which children blow dried peas.

clue.text: Try carrying long box exported from India?

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: to test is to try out
to long for is to ache for

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to carry a lengthy crate shipped from India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' looks like an adjective for the box but is the verb, to yearn. The question mark marks the definition as a description: such chests carried tea from India.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea chests are light wooden crates in which tea was shipped from India and elsewhere.

clue.text: Farmer's tool in poor condition, loose at the edges

parts.note: sick means unwell, in poor condition

indicators.note: at the edges takes only the first and last letters of loose

explanation.surface: A farm implement is in bad shape and wobbly around the rim.
explanation.definitionFit: A sickle is a short-handled curved blade used for cutting crops.

clue.text: Clever sort swots up absorbing piece of literature?

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other
in a down clue, up means the word for swots is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to swot is to study hard, which is to cram
a tale is a story, a piece of literature

explanation.surface: Studious types revise thoroughly while soaking up a set text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads the swotting word backwards (SMARC) in this down entry, and 'absorbing' takes the story inside. A swot is British slang for a pupil who studies hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart alec is a know-all, someone irritatingly clever.

clue.text: Be source of inspiration for puzzle

parts.note: a muse is a person or spirit inspiring an artist

explanation.surface: To inspire someone is also to baffle them.
explanation.definitionFit: To bemuse is to confuse or bewilder.

clue.text: Rot even beginning to appear on two kinds of timber

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the letter above the timber words
beginning takes the opening letter of even

parts.note: yew is a kind of tree and wood
ash is another tree and wood

explanation.surface: Decay is starting to show even on two types of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rot' seems to be wood decay, but it is the sense of nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash means nonsense or humbug, which is what rot means in speech.

clue.text: Heir to throne shortened snazzy blue garment

parts.note: Chas is the short form of Charles, heir to the throne when this puzzle was set

indicators.note: snazzy means flashy, a signal to jazz up the letters of blue

explanation.surface: Prince Charles wears a short, bright blue garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A chasuble is the sleeveless outer vestment worn by a priest celebrating Mass.

clue.text: Reception area in Prague hotel, you say?

indicators.note: you say signals that the words are to be heard rather than read

parts.note: a hotel in Prague is a Czech inn

explanation.surface: Where guests arrive at a hotel in Prague.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'Czech inn' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A check-in is the desk where arriving guests or passengers register.

clue.text: In a way, chopped herb will do for Italian dish

indicators.note: in means put inside, so the shortened herb goes within the road word

parts.note: a lane is a way or road

indicators.note: chopped means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: sage is a herb

explanation.surface: A recipe says sliced herbs will serve for an Italian meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped' drops the herb's last letter, giving SAG. 'a' and 'will do for' are only link words, though 'a' looks like it should supply a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is an Italian baked dish of flat pasta sheets layered with sauce.

clue.text: Military unit's indifference

definitions.meaning: a body of troops sent away on a separate task
lack of feeling or interest, aloofness

explanation.definitionFit: A detachment is a group of soldiers sent on a special mission, and also emotional aloofness.

clue.text: Husband's restless desire creating problem

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
an itch is a restless craving

explanation.surface: A husband's urge to wander leads to trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitch is a snag or temporary difficulty.

clue.text: Girl seen entering stadium emirates stadium

indicators.note: entering means the name goes into the words emirates stadium, sitting across them

explanation.surface: A girl is spotted going into the Emirates Stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: The Emirates Stadium is Arsenal's football ground in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Tess is a girl's name, as in Hardy's Tess of the d'Urbervilles.

clue.text: Film about origins of an old Marxist supporter

indicators.note: about means around, so the haze word goes round the letters

parts.note: a film is a thin layer or haze, a mist

indicators.note: origins of picks the first letters of an and old

explanation.surface: A movie about the beginnings of an old Marxist sympathiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' seems a movie, but it is a thin haze.
explanation.definitionFit: A Maoist follows Mao Zedong's Chinese form of Marxist communism.

clue.text: Crimes not well received by men in charge

indicators.note: received by means taken inside, so the second piece goes within the first

parts.note: kings are rulers, men in charge
ill means not well

explanation.surface: Wrongdoing is greeted badly by the bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: Killings are murders, the gravest of crimes.

clue.text: Child at home twice given toast

indicators.note: twice says the pair of pieces is written two times over

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A child at home is given buttered toast two times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toast' looks like bread, but it is the drinking salute.
explanation.definitionFit: Chin-chin is an informal drinking salute, like cheers.

clue.text: Hit on head, officer dropped

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for commanding officer
shed means dropped, as leaves are

explanation.surface: An officer is struck on the head and falls.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosh is to strike someone with a short heavy club, usually on the head.
